issue_context.title: Default value of `CollisionShape3D`'s property `debug_color` should not be saved in .tscn file
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.4.dev6

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev6 - Windows 10.0.22631 - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF (20 threads)

### Issue description

The default value of `CollisionShape3D`'s property `debug_color` (introduced in 4.4.dev6) should not be saved in `.tscn` file.
Not friendly to Version Control.

comments: The default is configured differently, as an empty `Color`, I think there's an inconsistency between the default value and the revert here that breaks this

* See #39072.

`_validate_property()` is missing. I'll take a look.

review_comments:
```suggestion
```
Generally the form AFAIK and to me is more readable

When spanning 50+ lines and multiple functions, I tend to prefer it with some spacing, as otherwise the start and end of the scope can be hard to spot at a glance.

Not a policy but I wouldn't go out of our ways to point out such things either in style reviews, unless it's inconsistent with surrounding code.
That's fair, I find it easier to read myself when it's attached and it's AFAIK the majority of existing code but good points
* Probably these `#ifdef`s were not needed at all, see #100317. But I was too late to answer here.

Wouldn't it be better to keep `Color()` (black) instead of transparent black as the fallback?

If using collision shapes without a scene tree, a black shape is probably better than a transparent one.

This is debatable. On the one hand, at least you'll see the shape. On the other hand, you might get a bunch of indistinguishable black rectangles, squares, spheres, etc. But in any case, this is a very hypothetical scenario, the vast majority of users use the standard `SceneTree`, and do not implement their own `MainLoop`s.

This transparent black already got noticed by a user of my voxel terrain module. They then though collision didn't work, but then we figured out it's because of the default value. Our system doesn't use nodes so we then had to add code to grab the debug_color from SceneTree.
Would you prefer transparent or black color?

Why can't we use a fallback value that's actually a good option, like the current default?
```
1837:   debug_collisions_color = GLOBAL_DEF("debug/shapes/collision/shape_color", Color(0.0, 0.6, 0.7, 0.42));
```

I think it's fine if hardcoded and not following user config as it's for more niche use cases, though from the report we got so far, more users seem to be affected by the transparent fallback that we thought.

Is this an issue this PR already addresses though, making all projects using SceneTree have the proper color (as opposed to only projects using shape nodes)?
I would be for a better default too, although having skimmed over some code related to it, I think it's been used as a special value to mean "null". Maybe that should be checked as well
